title: Understanding the organization and its context
summary: Know the internal and external issues that affect what your QMS can achieve, including whether climate change is relevant.
evidence: Context register with issues and review date; climate determination with reasons; review at management review.

title: Needs and expectations of interested parties
summary: Identify who has a stake in your QMS, what they require, and which of those requirements your QMS addresses.
evidence: Interested-party register showing requirements and which are addressed through the QMS.

title: Scope of the QMS
summary: Decide and write down what the QMS covers: products, services, sites, and any requirement you treat as not applicable, with reasons.
evidence: Scope statement (documented information) with justification for any non-applicable requirement.

title: QMS and its processes
summary: Define the processes the QMS needs, how they connect, who owns them, and how you control and measure them.
evidence: Process map and process cards; procedures or instructions needed to run processes; records that processes run as planned.

title: Leadership and commitment
summary: Top management takes accountability for the QMS and promotes a quality culture and ethical behavior.
evidence: Management review minutes, culture and ethics statement, concern log, evidence of leaders' involvement.

title: Customer focus
summary: Leaders make sure customer and legal requirements are understood and met and customer satisfaction stays a priority.
evidence: Customer satisfaction results and actions; KPI reviews; complaint handling.

title: Quality policy
summary: Set a quality policy that fits your context and strategic direction, communicate it, and make it available.
evidence: Approved policy (documented information), communication records, availability to interested parties.

title: Roles, responsibilities and authorities
summary: Assign and communicate who is responsible for what in the QMS, including keeping the QMS intact during change.
evidence: Role profiles or RACI tables, organization chart, appointment of responsibilities.

title: Determining risks and opportunities
summary: Use your context and interested parties to identify risks and opportunities the QMS must address.
evidence: Risk and opportunity registers linked to context issues.

title: Actions to address risks
summary: Analyze and evaluate risks and take actions proportionate to their impact.
evidence: Risk register with ratings, actions, owners and effectiveness review.

title: Actions to address opportunities
summary: Analyze and evaluate opportunities separately and decide which to pursue.
evidence: Opportunity register with decisions and results.

title: Quality objectives
summary: Set measurable objectives at relevant functions and plan what, who, when and how results are evaluated.
evidence: Objectives with targets, plans and progress (documented information).

title: Planning of changes
summary: Plan changes to the QMS in a controlled way: purpose, consequences, resources, communication, and review of results.
evidence: Change planning records, communication and post-change review.

title: Resources, people, infrastructure, environment
summary: Provide the people, infrastructure and work environment the processes need.
evidence: Resource plans in management review; maintenance records; work environment provisions.

title: Monitoring and measuring resources
summary: Keep measuring equipment suitable, calibrated or verified, identified and protected; act if it is found out of calibration.
evidence: Calibration register and certificates; basis for calibration where no standard exists; out-of-tolerance assessments.

title: Organizational knowledge
summary: Identify the knowledge needed to run processes and achieve results, then retain, apply and share it.
evidence: Knowledge map, lessons learned, key-person risk actions.

title: Competence
summary: Define required competence for each role, close gaps through training or other actions, and evaluate effectiveness.
evidence: Training matrix, qualifications, training records and effectiveness checks (documented evidence).

title: Awareness
summary: Make sure people know the policy, objectives, their contribution, quality culture and ethics, and the consequences of not following the QMS.
evidence: Awareness session records, quiz results, induction records.

title: Communication
summary: Decide what, when, with whom and how to communicate internally and externally about the QMS.
evidence: Communication plan or matrix; meeting records.

title: Documented information
summary: Create, approve, update and control documents and records so the right version is available and protected.
evidence: Document master list, approval and revision records, retention list, access controls.

title: Operational planning and control
summary: Plan and control the processes needed to deliver products and services, including outsourced ones.
evidence: Control plans, work instructions, records that processes were carried out as planned.

title: Requirements for products and services
summary: Communicate with customers (including contingency information), determine requirements, review them before committing, and manage changes.
evidence: Contract or order review records, records of changed requirements, contingency information given to customers.

title: Design and development
summary: Plan and control design: inputs, controls, outputs and changes. Not applicable if you do not design.
evidence: Design plans, input records, reviews, verification and validation, design change records.

title: Control of externally provided processes, products and services
summary: Evaluate, select, monitor and re-evaluate suppliers, and tell them your requirements.
evidence: Supplier evaluations, approved supplier list, performance monitoring, purchase requirements.

title: Control of production and service provision
summary: Run production or service under controlled conditions: information, equipment, competent people, validation where needed.
evidence: Work instructions, job records, process validation where output cannot be verified.

title: Identification, traceability, property, preservation, post-delivery
summary: Identify outputs and their status, trace where required, care for customer property, preserve product and meet post-delivery needs.
evidence: Traceability records, customer property records, post-delivery activity records.

title: Control of changes
summary: Review and control unplanned production or service changes and record the results.
evidence: Change records with review results, who authorized and actions.

title: Release of products and services
summary: Verify requirements are met before release and record who authorized it.
evidence: Release records with conformity evidence and authorizing person.

title: Control of nonconforming outputs
summary: Identify and control nonconforming outputs; correct, segregate, inform or accept under concession.
evidence: NC records: description, actions, concessions, authority for the decision.

title: Monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation
summary: Decide what to monitor, how and when, and evaluate QMS performance and effectiveness.
evidence: KPI dashboard, analysis results (documented evidence).

title: Customer satisfaction
summary: Monitor customers' perception of how well their needs are met.
evidence: Survey results, analysis and actions.

title: Analysis and evaluation
summary: Analyze data to evaluate conformity, satisfaction, performance, risk actions, suppliers and improvement needs.
evidence: Analysis reports feeding management review.

title: Internal audit
summary: Run a planned audit program with objectives, criteria and scope; report results and act on findings.
evidence: Audit program, plans with objectives, reports and findings (documented evidence).

title: Management review
summary: Top management reviews the QMS at planned intervals with all required inputs and records decisions.
evidence: Management review minutes covering all inputs and outputs (documented evidence).

title: Continual improvement
summary: Use results, analysis and review outputs to improve the QMS and its results.
evidence: Improvement projects and their results; opportunity register.

title: Nonconformity and corrective action
summary: React to nonconformities, find root causes, act, check effectiveness and update risks if needed.
evidence: Nonconformity and corrective action records with root cause and effectiveness verification.
